newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW - Cemex domestic sales seen up.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Cemex domestic sales seen up.

text.p: The Mexican unit of cement maker, Cemex, said on Friday that its domestic sales could rise 5.8 percent to 14.0 million tonnes in 1997 compared to the 13.223 million tonnes produced in 1996.

The company said that its exports in 1997 may decline 16.4 percent compared to the year before to 3.6 million tonnes, due to an increase in installed capacity in Asia that has knocked down demand for imports.
Domestic tonnage, together with exports from Mexico, will give the company an installed capacity of 70 percent, Cemex director of planning, Francisco Cue, told Reuters in an interview.
The Mexican unit of Cemex, with 18 plants, contributed 44 percent of company revenues in 1996 and 54 percent of consolidated group cash flow.
Together with an increase in tonnage in Mexico, Cemex forecasts stable average realized prices, which "should be at least at the rhythm of inflation," Cue said.

He said that the weakness in prices in the first quarter pf 1997, noted by analysts, is relative, since "in December 1996, (prices) were 75 dollars, in January they were almost 80 dollars and in February equal to January."
The average billed price estimated by Cemex for 1997 could reach $90 a tonne, but "easily at a minimum of $85," he said.
Any erosion in cement prices in Mexico should be measured against increases in the price of fuels and electric energy, he said.

"Definitely if there is an important difference between inflation and our costs.... This year we will see a real increase of more or less 10 percent in the price of fuel and about a real 50 percent in energy," he said.
To meet these rising costs, Cemex Mexico will aim to maintain a high participation in markets to reach a rate of capacity utilization that will allow it to have profitable margins, he said.
Cemex, which is traditionally better positioned in the formal construction sector, dedicated itself in 1996 to expanding its presence in the informal sector.
Last year, it started 1,000 new sales points in the country and in October launched a new presentation of its 25 kilogram sacks.
According to Cue, the company calculates that in 1997 it could move a million tonnes of cement in the new presentation.
"The introduction of a 25 kilograms size, which is already at a national level, will give us an additional two percentage points in our global participation in the market," he said.
He said that Cemex is the only cement company in Mexico to offer this presentation, whose packaging implies an additional cost of about $1.30 (10 pesos) per tonne.
Cemex estimates 1997 domestic cement consumption at 23 million tonnes, of which 10.5 to 11 million tonnes will be in the informal sector.
